approaches.name: Count, then sort the distinct values
approaches.intuition: A frequency table plus a sort with a two-part key gives the ranking directly.
approaches.time: O(n + d log d) where d is the number of distinct values

approaches.name: Count, then a heap of size k
approaches.intuition: When `k` is much smaller than the number of distinct values, keep only the best `k` in a heap instead of sorting everything.
steps: Push `(count, -value)` pairs into a min-heap, popping when it grows past `k`
Read the heap in descending order
pitfalls: The tie-break: smaller values come first, so the heap key must reflect it (negate the value in a min-heap).
`k` is at most the number of distinct values, so the heap is never short.

talkTrackMd: Start with counting. Then compare sorting all distinct values with a bounded heap and state when each wins. Mention bucket sort by frequency as an O(n) alternative.
